chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Bird in the Earl Hines band and the origin of bop story
summary: Parker slept on the bandstand in stocking feet; Willard relays Hines's remark on bop's origin.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Didn't he work in Earl Hines' band at the same time Dizzy did?
Earl Hines told me that where bop came from, it was Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker playing their exercise books backwards in their dressing room to kill time.
When I told Dizzy that he got mad.

So Charlie would go to sleep on the bandstand with his shoes off, and they'd have to nudge him for his solo, and he'd walk out to the mike in his stocking feet. And people would just laugh. They thought it was part of the act, you know. He'd go back to his seat and go back to sleep. And he was playing tenor in that band. He wasn't playing alto.
a no, they played flute exercises
